nodes.title: Important Note
widgets_values:
> BFS Shot Planner — Optional
  >
  > This node was designed to simplify processing longer videos by splitting them into smaller shots. It also provides tools for prompt generation, subject segmentation, masks, cropping, uncropping, reference descriptions, and shot-by-shot
  > configuration.
  >
  > The planner is optional. If you prefer, you can use ComfyUI’s native Load Video nodes and limit the input to a maximum of 15 seconds, using a frame count supported by the model. In that setup, pass the input video through Add Guide instead
  > of the conventional native reference-video conditioning. The body or character reference should still be supplied as an image through the native reference node.
  >
  > One of the planner’s main advantages is its automatic loop: a single workflow run processes every configured shot and performs the swap sequentially. You can also configure the continuity/history window, which passes extra frames from the
  > previous generated shot into the next one to improve motion and visual continuity.
  >
  > Some variation between shots is still expected. This is especially noticeable when the character reference shows only part of the body, because the model may generate unseen clothing or body details differently in each shot. A clear full-
  > body reference generally improves consistency.
  >
  > You can review and edit the character description extracted from the reference image. This also allows you to request details that are not visible in the original reference, such as roller shoes, accessories, clothing changes, or other
  > character features. This feature is still experimental and has not been explored extensively.

The guide video provides the scene and the performance: its background, environment, lighting, camera, framing, body pose, hand and arm movement, head rotation, gaze direction, lip movement and facial expression, frame by frame; only the main subject of the guide video is replaced: its face, hair, body and clothing become <Subject 1>.  summary: [video generation + reference] Replace the guide subject with <Subject 1>, keeping the scene, camera and the complete motion and performance of the guide video.  detailed_description: [Shot 1] <Subject 1> takes the exact place of the guide subject and moves with the same timing, body pose, gestures, head motion, gaze, speech and facial expressions, while keeping the complete look from <Picture 1>: head, face, skin, hair or fur, body shape and clothing stay stable in every frame, with no trace of the original subject's face, hair or clothing. nodes.title: Aiorbust
widgets_values:
# AIORBUST
## MiniMax H3  -  Character Swap
Puts the person from **your photos** into **any video**, keeping its motion, camera and room.

**You need:** 1 video  +  1 full-body photo  +  1 close-up of the face.

**Follow the orange STEP notes, left to right:**
1-3  Shot Planner: video, shots, your two photos
4  Head Swap LoRA (switch on the right)
5  Swap settings + seed
6  Queue

nodes.title: HOW TO USE  -  steps 1 to 3 (Shot Planner)
widgets_values:
## STEP 1  -  Video  (Shot Planner, 🎞 Video tab)
Pick or upload the video whose **motion** you want. Set the **Range** if you only want part of it. Up to **15 s per shot**.

## STEP 2  -  Shots  (🎬 Shots tab)
One clip, no camera cuts, under 15 s: leave it as **one shot**. Longer or with cuts: **Split into shots** - one run swaps them all and joins them back.

## STEP 3  -  Your person  (📝 Prompts & refs tab)
Set the references for **every shot (global)**:
- **click** a photo = **ref** -> the **full-body** photo (outfit + body)
- **shift + click** = **ref 2** -> a **close-up of the face** (identity). **Without it only the clothes change.**

More than one person in the video? **👥 People & masks** tab -> *Who is replaced*.

nodes.title: STEP 4  -  Head Swap LoRA
widgets_values:
## STEP 4  -  Head Swap LoRA
Leave it **ON** (switch next to the Aiorbust note at the top, or this group's toggle).
It sharpens the face shape so it matches your close-up. Strength **0.5**.

Turn it **off** only if the face starts to look stiff or over-done.

nodes.title: STEP 5  -  Swap settings + seed
widgets_values:
## STEP 5  -  Swap settings (Conditioning node, highlighted)
Keep these - they are what make the **face** swap:
- `use_ref_2` = **true** (uses the close-up)
- `ref_image_size` = **max**
- `source_blur` = **head + hands (keep mouth)** - hides the original face so it is not copied

**Seed** (highlighted): same seed = same take. Not happy? **Change the seed first** before touching anything else.

nodes.title: STEP 6  -  Queue + results
widgets_values:
## STEP 6  -  Queue
Check the **▶ Run** tab of the Shot Planner for warnings, then press **Queue**.

Results land in **ComfyUI/output**:
- the swapped video
- a **side-by-side** (original | references | result) to judge it

nodes.title: VIDEO LONGER THAN 15 SECONDS
widgets_values:
## Longer than 15 s?
The model makes **max ~15 s at a time**, so the planner cuts the video into **shots** and swaps them one after another in **one Queue**.

1. **🎞 Video**: load the full video (Range = the part you want).
2. **🎬 Shots**: **Split into shots** - it finds the camera cuts. Keep every shot **≤ 15 s**; use split / merge / skip on each shot.
3. **📝 Prompts & refs**: set ref + ref 2 as **global**, so every shot gets the same person.
4. Leave **Continuity** on - it feeds the end of each shot into the next so she stays consistent.
5. **Queue once.** All shots render in turn and are joined into one video (~2 min per shot on a 5090).

nodes.title: LOW VRAM  (under 32 GB)
widgets_values:
## Low VRAM? (tested on 32 GB - smaller cards: start here, in this order)
1. **Turn ON the two memory nodes in group 4**: *MiniMax Low VRAM Attention* and *MiniMax Chunk FeedForward* (select -> **Ctrl+B**). Same output, lower peak memory. More chunks = less memory, a little slower.
2. **Shorter shots**: in the Shot Planner **🎬 Shots** tab, lower the max shot length (e.g. 5-8 s instead of 15). A short clip just becomes 2-3 shots - still one Queue, joined at the end.
3. **Smaller video**: lower **Megapixels** in the Shot Planner (0.5 now -> try 0.3). Smaller output, much less memory.
4. Start ComfyUI with **--reserve-vram 2** (or **--lowvram** as a last resort), and close other apps using the GPU.

Out of memory error? Go one step further down this list and Queue again.
